title: छाउघर उपन्यासमा मानसिक सङ्घात
authors: अधिकारी थापा Adhikari Thapa, सीता Sita
nepali: यस लेखको प्रमुख उद्देश्य समसामयिक विषयमा राज सरगमद्वारा लिखित छाउघर उपन्यासको पात्रको मानसिक अभिघातका बारेमा विश्लेषण गर्नु रहेको छ । साहित्यमा मनोविश्लेषणको सिद्धान्तद्वारा मानिसका विविध मनोदशा एवम् मनोसंरचनाको खोजअन्वेषण गर्ने फ्रायडीय शास्त्रीय परम्परा अत्यन्त प्रचलित देखिन्छ । यसै मनोविज्ञानसँग नै सम्बन्ध राख्दै नवीन उत्तरआधुनिक सांस्कृतिक समालोचना चिन्तन पद्धतिको रूपमा विकसित हुँदै आएको उत्तरसंरचनावाद र नवमनोविश्लेषणात्मक सिद्धान्तको एउटा सशक्त मान्यता अभिघात पनि हो । प्राचीन कालदेखि नै शस्त्राभिघात र आत्माभिघातबाट मानिस पीडित बनिरहेको यथार्थलाई विश्वसाहित्य र नेपाली साहित्यमा पनि प्रशस्त उतारिँदै आएको छ । नेपाली साहित्यमा नारी समस्यामूलक उपन्यासहरू लेखिने क्रममा एउटा दरिलो उपस्थिति जनाउने छाउघर उपन्यासले प्राकृतिक रूपमा नारीजातिमा हुने एउटा शारीरिक जैविक परिवर्तनको अपरिहार्य प्रक्रिया रजस्वलालाई मूल समस्या वा विषयका रूपमा उठान गरेको छ ।सामाजिक सांस्कृतिक आधारमा गरिने नारीमाथिको लैङ्गिक विभेदकारी छाउप्रथाले उनीहरू सानैदेखि शारीरिक र मानसिक अभिघातको सिकार भएका तथ्यहरू छन् । प्रथम पटक रजस्वला भएर अचानक छाउगोठको कठीन पीडादायी र लामो अनुभव भोग्नुपर्दा एक अबोध बालिकाको मानसिकतामा उब्जिएका अनगिन्ती जिज्ञासा, भयग्रस्त वेदना र आक्रोसका एवम् उसमाथि परेका मानसिक सङ्घातकासाथै यसैकारण सिर्जित महिलामाथिका लैङ्गिक हिंसाको विविध समस्यालाईउपन्यासमा सशक्त ढङ्गले प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । यस लेखमा यही अभिघात सिद्धान्तलाई आधार बनाई छाउघर उपन्यासका प्रमुख पात्रको मानसिक सङ्घातको अध्ययन विश्लेषण गरिएको छ ।
american_english: The main objective of this article is to analyze the psychological trauma of a character in the novel 'Chauharko Ghar' written by Raj Saragam. This analysis focuses on contemporary issues. Freud's psychoanalytic theory and the concept of trauma are used to explore human emotions and mental conditions. Various forms of psychoanalysis, including traditional Freudian approaches and newer postmodern critiques, are examined. Literature showing how people suffer from trauma, both physical and mental, from ancient times to now, is reviewed. In Nepali literature, novels dealing with women's issues show a significant presence of 'Chauharko Ghar,' which naturally highlights menstruation as a main problem. The social and cultural practice of 'chaupadi'—discrimination against women during menstruation—has led to physical and psychological trauma for women and girls. This harmful tradition causes countless suffering and trauma. A young, innocent girl suddenly experiences severe pain and goes through a difficult, painful, and long experience in 'chaupadi gotho' (menstrual hut). This leads to many questions, fears, and painful memories in her mind, causing significant psychological trauma. The article analyzes this psychological trauma using trauma theory. The analysis covers the young girl's mental state before the trauma, the trauma itself, and her mental state after the trauma. The study reveals that trauma affects not only the victim's body and mind but also their relationships with family, society, and the outside world. This analysis is based on the novel 'Chauharko Ghar.' {The main objective of this article is to analyze the psychological trauma of a character in the novel 'Chauharko Ghar' written by Raj Saragam. british_english: This article's primary goal is to investigate the psychological impact on a character within Raj Saragam's novel 'Chauharko Ghar', with a focus on modern issues. The study utilises Freud's psychoanalytic framework and trauma theory to examine human emotions and mental states. It explores various psychoanalytic methodologies, ranging from conventional Freudian interpretations to contemporary postmodern critiques. The article surveys literary works that document the experience of trauma, encompassing both physical and psychological dimensions, across different historical periods. Within Nepali literature, novels addressing women's concerns frequently feature 'Chauharko Ghar', thereby foregrounding menstruation as a central theme. The traditional social and cultural practice of 'chaupadi', which involves the ostracisation of women during menstruation, has resulted in both physical and psychological trauma for females and young girls. This detrimental custom inflicts considerable suffering and trauma upon its victims. A young, innocent girl unexpectedly endures intense pain and undergoes a arduous, distressing, and protracted experience within the 'chaupadi gotho' (menstrual hut), engendering numerous inquiries, apprehensions, and agonizing recollections that precipitate substantial psychological trauma. The article employs trauma theory to dissect this psychological trauma, examining the young girl's mental condition prior to the trauma, the trauma itself, and her psychological state subsequent to the trauma. The investigation uncovers that trauma has repercussions not solely on the victim's physique and psyche but also on their affiliations with family, society, and the external world. This analysis is grounded in the novel 'Chauharko Ghar'. {This article's primary goal is to investigate the psychological impact on a character within Raj Saragam's novel 'Chauharko Ghar', with a focus on modern issues.
